### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">section 2 of chapter 5: Neil had no chance of missing the bus in the morning, he simply hadn’t slept. He’d laid in bed replaying the events of the last five years in his head, snippets of thoughts flashing in and out of his mind’s eye in the half awake, half sleeping hours before the sun rose.
It was old territory, nothing he hadn’t done countless time in jail. He thought he might leave it behind when he finally got free, he was wrong, it followed him.
The bus was almost full by the time it got to his building, he didn’t feel like talking to anyone so he’d waiting in his apartment until it had arrived. Neil was in no mood for socialising this morning.
He sat in an empty row on a few rows behind the driver, hoping that he was the last onto the bus.
He wasn’t, just as the bus doors closed a tall, wiry man burst through the front doors of the apartment building yelling “Wait, Wait…’ and sprinted after the bus that was already gaining speed to it’s next destination.
The bus driver swore and slammed on the breaks, jolting everyone on board forward violently, the bus passengers universally responded with a chorus of profane complaining.
In the row behind him a passenger, a large man easily out weighing Niel by fifty pounds of muscle yelled “Hey Mike, where’d you learn to drive… you owe me a coffee”
There was a round of agreement.
The man caught up to the bus and jumped through the doors thanking the bus driver profusely “Hey Mike, thanks man, you know I’m never late, I owe you one!”
Mike “Be on time, there won’t be a next time”
The man looked around and saw the empty seat next to Neil
Shit.
The passenger behind Neil was still grumbling along with some others about the sudden stop. He said to the man as he got to Jims seat
“Hey man, you’d better not be late again, now you owe me a coffee!”
The man calmly stared him down and coldly said “Tully, I don’t owe you anything, last I remebered you owed me something”
Tully, pushing back “I aint got nothing for you and do owe you shit”
The man still standing in the aisle as the bus was pulling away from the curb again sighed “Ok Tully, some people will be dissapointed, but hey it’s your choice”
Tully paled slight at the mention of the other people. The bus was deadly quiet, all the passenger fixated on this confrontation. Neil was worried he’s end up in the middle of a brawl on his first full day out of prison.
Tully’s seat mate, nudged him “Tully, don’t it’s not a fight you want to pick”
Tully looked down, suddenly engrossed in his phone.
The man sat next to Neil and with a smile introduced himself “Hi friend, name’s Rook, not my real name but everyone calls me that”
Neil reluctantly engaged Rook, he nodded his head towards Tully sitting right behind them and said quietly “Is this going to a problem?”
Rook laughed “Nope, Tully’s all talk, we just had some business that he didn’t get around to finishing yet, don’t worry no brawl on the bus today”
Neil relaxed very slightly, still ready for something to kick off.
Rook continued thier conversation with far too much energy “So you’re new, when did you get out?”
Neil again reluctantly responded, this was exactly what he’d been hoping to avoid “Yesterday”
Rook blew out cheeks “Wow, total green! Don’t worry it’s a blur at first, but you get used to it. Though some days I can’t tell the difference between this and jail”
That did nothing to help Neils mood, he didn’t respond.
Rook looked appraisingly at Neil, nodded and said gently “Don’t want to chat this morning, no problems, I get we’ve all been there. Remember this, you need friends outside just like you did on the inside, if you ever want to chat, my name is Rook”
With that he put his head back and went to sleep.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Neil stares out the window, his eyes unfocused as his mind wanders not noticing as the the bus leaves the Outer’s grey suburbia, leaving behind block after block of squat apartment buildings, strips malls and entertainment centres. 
The bus passed over the long viaduct that separated the Rust Belt factories and warehouses from the city’s edge.
The viaduct was three lanes in each direction and arrow straight for at least two miles as it passed over a vast flood plain, the result of a past environmental catastrophe from before the Reclamation.
Neil had never been here, it was always out of sight and out of mind for a Level 7 in his former life, of course he knew about the Rust Belt, it was storied history that the factories here helped rebuild the Bi-Continental Government of the Americas after international trade collapsed.
They had passed over the viaduct now into Rust Belt proper, miles upon miles of mega factories and warehouses, with business parks of holding hundreds of smaller factories and warehouses. 
Unlike the grey and grime of the Outer’s suburbia, there was colour here, the buildings were bright and clean with corporate logos, company colours and murals splashed across the huge walls. The lawns  and gardens lining the driveway in to each building were green and well maintained
Corporations always want to look good Neil thought.
Rook was awake and had been watching Neil look out through the window as if appraising him, he match Neil’s gaze “Yep, here it is, the beating heart of the country, the place that makes everything and saved us all. Look at all that money just oozing out of every building… and we here on this bus keep it all ticking along.
Neil didn’t respond, instead he kept surveying the scenery… he recognised some the names, they were suppliers he’d used.
Rook didn’t let Neil’s lack of response stop him “You know without us 3’s and 4’s nothing would get made, the whole world needs us to be exactly where we are”
Neil wasn’t used to this kind of talk and the inference annoyed him, he looked at Rook who was smiling expansively.“That’s not true at all, I built things, lots of things before…”
Rook interrupted, ice in eyes “Sorry to burst you’re bubble Neil, you built with the supplier we created out here, without us you would have made exactly zero.
What Neil thought, Rook’s used of his name was a shock “I didn’t think I gave you my name”
Rook steely eyes didn’t waver as he stared right through Neil “Neil, I knew who you were before you even arrived at you’re apartment last night, in fact people I know were watching your trial… like I said you need friends out here, and I think I you and I can help each other”
Neil remembered how the bus silenced when Rook mentioned his friends was now genuinely worried “Look, I’m just here to do my time in probation and get back out into the world without any trouble”
Rook, laughed to cold glint in his eyes never leaving “Get back? what to Level 7? You’re stuck here like the rest of us. You think you’ll be able to pay off your Housing Loan, think they’ll let you get out of the grind. no my new friend they need us out here so they can sit in thier shiny glass towers and sip champagne.”
Neil wasn’t going to be stuck out here longer than necessary, he already had a plan in mind to get out. “Listen, Rook is it? I don’t know about you but I’m not some loser who’s stuck here, I’ll get back up and leave this place and people like you behind”
Rook shook his head in disappointment, like Neil had failed a test “five years in prison and you’ve still got the level 7 attitude, piece of advice from someone who knows keep that kind of talk under wraps”
The bus jerked to a stop and the PA system barked mechanically “destination reached, all off the bus”
Neil started to get up and Rook grabbed his arm, his grip was strong and practised, Neil couldn’t break it in the confined space of the seat row. Rook leaned in and said tightly “When you work out how fucked you are, I’ll be here”
Neil squeezed past and shook Rooks hand off his arm and marched off the bus with the rest of the passengers without looking back.</span></span></span></span>

He can see another bus coming up the road ready to dislodge it’s group of workers, if Neil could see further he’d see hundreds of similar busses ferrying workers in and out all day and night..
Confused as to what’s next, Neil awkwardly stands at the bus stop, “where the hell do I go” he thinks as he watches Rook walk away with a small group of workers to one of the factories.
One of his fellow passengers, a robust shorter man who seems to be dressed a bit better than the utilitarian work clothes everyone else, including Neil, are wearing. He approaches and shoots out a enthusiastic hand to shake “Neil? Neil Lucas?”
Neil responds as the man shakes his has hand wildly “Yes, that’s me”
“Excellent, I’m Knox, we didn’t get a chance to meet before you got on the bus…I’m your sponsor” Knox, still grasping Neil’s hand ushers his towards the only office building in the cul-de-sac. “This is us over here, you must have done something right, you’ve got a office job, just like me…”
Neil reclaiming his hand and walking with Knox towards the ten story glass office building, his mind trying to catch up asks “Sponsor, I’m sorry I don’t know anything about that”
Knox speeding up the pace and dragging Neil along says “They still tell you absolutely nothing when you leave prison, nothing ever changes. Don’t worry we’ll have time to talk about all of it today whilst we get you settled in”
Knox and Neil are in the HR department waiting room on the second floor, it’s stark and almost hospital like, the walls are a uniform beige dotted here and there with  low quality reprints of once famous landscapes. Neil is sitting one seat away from Knox on a harsh and unforgiving plastic chair, one of about half a dozen against the wall. 
It’s only Neil and Knox waiting, Neil figures by the wear on carpet this is a busy department. 
Knox sitting back like he’s preparing for a long wait starts talking “So, welcome to your new job, you hit the jackpot being qualified for an office job! I myself used to be an accountant before… all this” he waves around the room.
“I understand you were in construction before?”
Neil answered “Sort of, I used to own a construction business”
Knox said “That’sclose enough, from what I understand you’ve been allocated a project management job here, not many of those going around”
“I’m not really a project manager” said Neil.
Knox” It doesn’t matter, do your best”
Neil considered Knox’s statement, he wasn’t actually sure what he expected, but project management was something he probably could do, at least is wasn’t factory job.
“Neil ventured :you mentioned sponsor?”
Know smiled “Yes, more tour guide and mentor, just someone who knows the ropes and can help get newbies like you settled into thier new routine. Just think of me as your personal AI, since you can’t have one right now. Anything you need to know about life after prison I’m here to help”
Knox’s tone changed “Speaking of learning the rope, what was that with Rook when you got off the bus?”
Neil stiffened, he wasn’t sure anyone else had seen it “Nothing, just a misunderstanding”
Knox pressed “It didn’t look like nothing, Rook is not someone to have a problem with”
“You know him?” asked Neil.
Knox looked around, assured they were alone he spoke quietly “Rook is part of the Grey’s, they are not people you want to be associated with”
“Who are the Greys? I’ve never heard of them” Neil, curious.
Knox shifted over to the seat next to Neil and leaned in close, almost whispering “One of those things you never hear about in the city, the Greys are a group who opposes the system we live under, they’re always looking for ways to break it. They are not nice and quite a few people have been burnt by them, literally”
The thought of a under the radar group who wanted to break the system was a shock to Neils’ Level 7’s view of the world.
They were interrupted when the door to office opened abruptly, a very well dressed and presented lady barked “Neil, which one of you is Neil Lucas?”
Neil put his hand up.
“Come with me” as she retreated back into the office.
Neil followed her into the office, it was large and housed half a dozen workstations all occupied by office worked at thier terminals or on the phone. The buzz of activity was a stark contrast to the quiet of the waiting room.
She sat a her workstation and gestured to Neil to sit in the chair opposite her desk.
“Sorry about that, normally the waiting room is full and I have to make myself heard. I’m Eleanor, I’ll be getting you all set up with you r new job.”
Neil sensing she’s trying to be helpful “Nice to meet you Eleanor, I’m kind of in the dark about what is going on here”
She laughs “Well I’m here to help you out” looking at here terminal she clicks through a few screens. “Says here you used to own a construction company… perfect, we’ve got you a role as a Project Management assistant here, at Stratum Projects.
“Eleanor sees Neil’s reaction “Sorry, but that’s about as high as you can go being a Level 3, actually, it’s better than I’ve seen most get… you must have some friends out there somewhere.”
She continues “So, I need to tell you this not like a normal job. First, you’ve got be here on time at 8am, don’t miss the bus, and you’ll finish at 6pm each night. Yuu get Sundays off and for the next 12 months you’ll get no holidays.
Neil reacts angrily “Ten hours a day, six days a week? I was better off in prison!”
She moved forward over the top of Neil’s protest “Now if you’re late you’ll get penalised points same if your performance reviews are sub-standard… but this job will be easy enough for you so you shouldn’t have an issue”
Neil interrupted “…but I’ve done my time in prison, this seems completely unfair..”
Eleanor shakes her head at Neil “I’m going to have to remind you, you’re a Probationary Citizen, whilst you transition back to being an unrestricted citizen you’re not completely free, you better understand that really quick”
She continues, any of her goodwill towards Neil now long gone “So as a Probationary citizen you are not entitled to any salary over and above your Baseline credit allowance, we don’t do overtime here so they will be no extra work.
Eleanor checks a few boxes on the terminal and finally says “That’s it Mr Lucas, you can go now, Knox will get you situated in the office, if you have any questions about your employment here be sure to address them with your direct Manager, good bye and best of luck to you.”
He was dismissed.
Neil left the office without another word, fuming, the anger he pushed down last night flaring back hotter than ever. “I’m just a fucking slave here” he thought, as the realisation sunk in that he might just be stuck here forever.</span></span></span></span>

Section 4, Subsection 4 – Temporary Status –  (A) Disruptive Person
1.1 The designation of Disruptive Person can be applied to any citizenship level.
1.2 Such a designation will be applied to a Citizen who displays either: a single severe anti-social behavior incident as reported by no less than 10 other citizens, or at least 3 incidents of anti-social behavior as reported by no less than 5 other citizens.
1.3 A Citizen will be designated a Disruptive Person for a period of 12 months.
1.4 Designation as a Disruptive Person does not alter Citizen’s status points or level.
1.5 A Disruptive Person will accrue penalty points a 2x the normal rate for the period of the designation.
1.6 If a Disruptive Person has an anti-social incident as reported by no less than 5 other citizen during the 12 month period, the citizen will be automatically re-designated a Level 3 - Probationary Citizen (Temporary).</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">This was the day he’s been working towards almost his entire life, chasing down every points hack and social credit program he could find. All the relentless networking and arse kissing higher levels had paid off. 
Today was the day Jim left Level 7 behind and assumed his new life fully as a Level 8 Full Citizen. 
Today, Jim was leaving the Landis Corporation for good and starting as the new VP of Private Client Business at Nova Corp.
Sarah had been busy getting Jim’s wardrobe ready all week, Jim was impressed how quickly she got the tailor to make his new suit, it had arrived just three days after the fitting. Helen put her onto the tailor, the same one Shane used, she was just as excited as Sarah was. 
It was perfectly tailored to fit Jim’s lean but athletic six foot frame, not a crease or seam out of place. It was a real merino wool in a charcoal grey with a subtle pin stripe.
Sarah had matched it with a new real cotton white shirt and a gold silk tie.
“Gold for success and luck today” She has dais as he left for work.
The news of his signing had hit Landis almost immediately and they had arranged a big farewell this morning before his start at Nova Corp. Jim couldn’t help think that the farewell morning tea was as much for their benefit as his. He knew all to well how important making friends with higher levels was.
Jim was relaxing with his EV in auto-drive, as was his habit, putting together in his head a few kind and humble words for his old team, his heart wasn’t in it as he really just wanted to move on and forget them. They’re just stepping stones, he thought, necessary evils on my path to the top. He admonished himself, he’d better make it good, there would be no more repeats of the arrogance he showed at Apex, that could have really blown up in his face. But I’m level 8 now, I’m untouchable. Luckily Shane’s points lawyer had made sure the incident ever saw light of day again.
His phone rang, it was the car dealership.
“Hello” Jim answered
“Good morning Mr Dalton, this is Jackson the sales Manager at Citadel Prestige”
“Hi Jackson, good to chat to you again, have you got news?” Jim asked.
“I do Mr Dalton we’ve been able to find a current year Lumora model 9 in the slate grey with light tan interior, however it will take about a week to get here from another dealer”
“Excellent news, I’m glad you could find one, I was worried I’d have to buy a slot in production line six months down the track!” Jim was beaming at this news. 
“Well we do aim to satisfy our clientele Mr Dalton, if you’d like to drop into the dealership anytime in the next few days with your current vehicle we’ll do an appraisal on it and we can also sign the contact in person” Jackson said smoothly.
“Sure, give me a day or tow and I’ll drop down” said Jim.
“One last item Mr Dalton, could you please authorise the deposit so we can secure the vehicle. As you know we will need a deposit of 50% which is 100,000 credits”
Jim sucked in a breath abruptly as the size of the deposit hit him. He’d only just received his first year’s 150,000 credits as a Level 8 a few days ago and he hadn’t started at Nova Corp yet.
“Approved” Jim said hesitantly, he’d never paid that much in one transaction, not even close.
“Thank you Mr Dalton, the deposit has cleared, look for to seeing you in few days”
Ouch.</span></span></span></span>

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">actually this is my wortld building on the tiers...:Level 10 – Elite Citizen – They very top 1%, C level managers, owners of major businesses, national politicians, industry leaders. The billionaire an multimillionaire class.
Level 9 – Model Citizen – getting to the top of the business and political world, the upper manager and successful business owners. You have to contribute quite a lot to society to be sitting at Level 9. For many they run almost two jobs, one thier business or political career the other managing all the areas to make up point across all their citizenship status. At this pont many have what are called CM’s or citizenship managers to keep keep them in this elevate level. At any one time only about 10% of citizen are at level 9, most people feeling the effort to get to this level too much work. Many entertainers sit here due to thier influence.
Level 8 – Full Citizen - This is the ultimate goal for people, to attain full citizenship as at this level you can vote and participate in politics. Generally you live a good upper middle class life with all you could want. Many people are happy to stay at this level as it is very comfortable. Middle and upper managers.
Level 7 – Unrestricted Citizen (Permanent) – This is where a good portion of the people end up, a comfortable life without out out trying too hard to climb the citizenship ladder. You get the next level of government handouts, you can get easy promotions up to lower middle management. You are reasonably well respected and have a buffer of points that is anything goes wrong you’re safe from dropping into the bottom 5 levels.
Level 6 – Unrestricted citizen (Probationary) – This is the level that all teenagers children turning 18 are automatically set at for 12 months until they earn start building up a profile to earn thier own points. It’s also the level that new citizens start at. Theoretically nothing is restricted to Level 6 citizen, however practically they are at the bottom of the list for pretty much everything.
Below the top 5 levels, where you absolutely don’t want to be, are the restricted levels where your rights and ability to work and live become more and more limited.
Level 5 – Restricted citizen (Temporary) Quite often new citizens or young people make mistakes, this level is considered a social “slap on the wrist” to get people onto the program of contributing to society. It’s normally a timed restriction for 3 or 6 months after which you’ve served your penalty and you revert back up to Level 6. Most people can ride it out without too much damage done to their lives.
Level 4 – Restricted Citizen (Permanent) whilst technically not permanent this level is for those who have repeatedly dropped below an acceptable level. Likely they’ve committed petty non-violent crimes that don’t give you jail sentences. These people are consistently going against the system.
Level 3 – Probationary Citizen (Temporary) Essentially reserved for those release from prison. These citizens are on probation for a period of 12 months, if no re-offending occurs then they are upgraded to Level 4 Restricted Citizen.
Level 2 - Incarcerated Citizen (Temporary) Status reserved for citizen who have been convicted of crimes and sent to jail.
Level 1 – Incarcerated Citizen (Permanent) Status reserved for citizens who have committed crimes where there is to be no chance of release from jail.
There is one last level, not often spoken of, or even known about by the average citizen.
Level 0 – non-citizen (Permanent) – at this point a person is basically removed from society, you cannot be employed, cannot have a bank account, you can’t travel or use any kind of transport, you can’t own property. You can’t even be homeless in the city as the Police will kick you out of the city or town limits.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">ok... my work for tonight, section 2 of chapter 6: The offices of Landis Corp felt different this morning, it was odd how much your perception could change in only a week. What he used to think of as a reasonably well appointed office space, where he had one of the better offices, just seemed worn and tacky now, like a veil had been lifted from hin vision showing him a reality he’d been avoiding.
Last week Jim was a valued member of the team, easily interacting with his peers, chatting with them with a relaxed ease, gossipping, joking, talking business without any barrier.
Today, that ease had gone. He was not one of the team. His work colleagues seemed oddly subdued around him, not unfriendly, but the casual camaraderie was gone. Conversations he’d had a mere 7 days ago were now forced, subtly calculated to curry favour with Jim in his new position.
Jim felt awkward, and he was glad this would be over soon. He just wanted to be done with this morning tea and move on to his new role at Nova Corp. 
He been to his new office only a few days ago to pick out some of the decorations for his new office. Calling it an office almost didn’t do it justice, it was on the corner of the 45th floor , just three levels down from the Executive clubhouse on the top floor of the Nova’s now building. The space was at least three times larger than what he was sitting now, no counting the large marble clad private bathroom complete with shower and walk in wardrobe. 
He picked out some tasteful original seascapes for the walls under the watchful eye of his new Executive Assistant and was keen to see if they’d match the paint colour he’d chosen.
He had to close off his work here first, and daydreaming about an office he could be in right now if he wasn’t wasting time.
Jim has one final email prepped and ready to send before the gathering in the Carter in ten minutes to say his official goodbyes. 
Sent, he logged off for a final time. 
Damn it he thought, he’d forgotten to attaching his working files.
Jim tried to log back in to the terminal
[User not Found – Please check Username of Password]
He didn’t type it wrong, after years logging in was muscle memory now, he tried again.
[User not Found – Please check Username of Password]
Had they off boarded him already? Jim guessed it didn’t really matter, they’ll find the data easily enough.
His phone chimed with a new message.
It was from his Personal Citizenship Points Portal.
“Dear Jim Dalton, we have completed the review of your warning: Anti-social Language in a public area and concluded the warning to be in error. 
In light of recent evidence provided by multiple parties the warning has been upgraded to: Serious Anti-social Language in a public area causing offence.
This warning carries a penalty of 500 citizenship points. 
Due to the serious nature of the offence, you have been designated a Disruptive Person
This designation multiplies the penalty to 1000 citizenship points.
You now have 4012 citizenship points,
You have been reallocated to Level 7.
There is no further appeal to this penalty. To view more details, log in to your portal.”
Jim’s world shook, he sat back down in the chair with a lifeless thud, his ears ringing and stars in his eyes, like he’d just been hit across the back of the head.
He was motionless, staring at the screen.
“This is not real” he thought “how can the be real?”
Rosalind the head of People and Culture knocked on his office door.
He hadn’t seen her approach, he’s hadn’t registered anything apart form the message on his phone, startled he looked up.
“Hi Jim, I think we’ll just cancel the farewell speech now, if you could make your way out of the office now please” Rosalind gestured out the door where two Landis security guards are waiting.
“You’re escorting me out, really?”
“I think its for the best Jim if you just go now” Rosalind says calmly.
Jim is getting angry now “I’ve been here over three years and you’re going to treat me like this?”
“Jim, you don;t work for Landis anymore, as of right now you’re trespassing, I can have these men make you leave, but I think we’d all prefer to avoid that” Rosalind said with a cold finality.
Jim, felt as if he was in a dream sleep walking out of the office, his brand new suit sitting heavy on him, his gold tie screaming of his failure as he walked by colleagues he’d know for years., He looked at them and they all turned thier faces away as he was escorted to the elevator.
Rosalind spoke as they waited for the lift. “Jim, these two will escort you to your car and let you our of the carpark, it’s my duty to inform you that you are no longer welcome in this building, please don’t return for any reason. If there are any personal items you have left behind be sure to email my department and we will ensure they are send out to you”
That was it, no good bye or good luck from people he’d worked with for years. 
The elevator arrived and Jim and the two security guards stepped into it, through the closing doors he could see that Rosalind had already turned her back on him.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Ok i'll give chapter 5 a bit more... in the meantime here's section 3 of chapter 6:Jim was sitting in his car silently, the leather seats and luxury trim a welcome familiarity that helped block out the outside world. 
He read and reread the message. It still didn’t seem real. Words kept repeating over and over again in his head.
Multiple sources, Serious Anti-social Language in a Public Area Causing Offence Disruptive Person.
He felt hollow as is the colour has been stripped away from him.
After a few minutes he signed and decided to deliberately change the way this day was going. He was going to fight this.
Jim dialled Shane’s number.
It didn’t ring, instead it went directly to a recorded message
“We’re Sorry, You Have Reached a Number That Has Been Disconnected or Is No Longer in Service”
What the hell?
He dialled Shane’s number three more times and three more time he heard the same automated message.
“We’re Sorry, You Have Reached a Number That Has Been Disconnected or Is No Longer in Service”
Jim’s newly found resolve cracked a little, Shane and his Lawyer were the first step to reversing all of this.
His personal AI chimed, he was due at Nova Corp in thirty minutes. 
Damn it, Jim realised he’d lost complete track of the time.
He called his new executive assistant.
The call was answered immediately “Nova Corp, Rachael speaking” 
Relieved this call was answered, Jim put on a cheerful voice said “Hi Rachael, It’s Jim Dalton here, just letting you know something came up and i’ll be a few minutes late for my induction meeting, if you could let Rob know please”
Silence on the other end of the call
“Hello?” Jim asked
“I’m so sorry Mr Dalton, I’ve been told to cancel all your appointments, please hold whilst I transfer your call” The line clicked over to hold music before Jim could say a word.
So, they know Jim thought as the soothing classical hold music played. 
He didn’t have to wait long, the call was answered by another professional female voice “Hello Mr Dalton, your speaking with Grace, Mr Hughes Assistant, what can I help you with today?”
Jim was taken a back by the question, it didn’t make any sense.
“Rob Hughes? is Rob available?” Jim asked
“Unfortunately Mr Hughes is unavailable, how can I help you?”
Again with the question, Jim’s mind was turning but unable to comprehended what was going on, he forced himself to clam down
“As I said to Rachael, I’m running a few minutes late for my first day there and just wanted to let Rob know, it took a bit longer than anticipated to say my goodbyes at my my old job” Jim was sweating.
“Mr Dalton, I don’t have you in the schedule for today, are you sure you have the right number?” Grace asked sweetly.
Rob answered his frustration a growing “Look I’m starting there today as the new VP of Private Client Business, Rob was going to show me around a get me introduced to everyone” 
“I’m sorry Mr Dalton there is nothing on the schedule like that today, I can assure you that if a new VP was coming onboard today I’d know about it, are you sure you know Mr Hughes?” Grace voice never wavered from corporate blandness.
“Well Grace, I can assure you I am starting today, Rob and I had lunch at apex last week and I signed the contract” Jim was starting to loose control.
“Mr Dalton, you’re getting quite agitated, please lower your voice. I’m looking at Mr Hughes calendar right now and he did not have lunch at Apex last week, furthermore a quick check of our staff portal shows no one under the name of Jim Dalton is employed here” Grace seemed to be losing her practiced patience just a little.
They’ve cut me loose, I’m not longer a Level 8 and they are denying it all thought Jim.
He didn’t have a response.
Grace asked “Mr Dalton, are you there?”
Jim answered, defeated “Yes, so I’m done there, before I even got started, is that how this is going to play out?”
Grace’s professionalism was back “I’m sorry Mr Dalton, it seems Nova Corp has no record of any dealings with you. Thank you for your time and have a great day!”
Jim didn’t bother hanging up, Grace cut the line as Jim dropped the phone into his lap and slumped back into the driver seat his eyes squeezed shut so hard he was seeing shapes in the darkness, his hand balled into fists pressing against this temples. 
Thankfully the one-way window tint didn’t didn’t allow anyone to see into the car.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">final section of chapter 5 : The first day went by in a flash, Neil wasn’t in the mood to be social but he forced himself to be. This was his life for the next twelve months one way or another so he’d just have to make the best of it.
Knox was a dutiful guide, he seemed to know everyone and wasn’t afraid to gossip about them behind their backs. Neil didn’t really listen, but he humoured Knox, Rook’s words “you need friends out here” still ringing in Neil’s ears.
The job was simple, Neil was going to be filing and doing general administrative jobs for the project management office. A glorified errand boy for people who knew far less about construction than Neil did.
Neil guessed they’d thought with his experience, he’d know his way around organising all the plans, manifests, quotes and surveys large construction projects would have. Thet weren’t wrong, he be able to the job with his eyes closed, and perhaps with a bit of spare time he could figure a way of getting out as quickly as possible.
He was one of five assistants to the project office, Knox had introduced him to all of them, but Neil has already forgotten thier names. Knox himself wasn’t one of them, he worked in different department completely.
Right on time the bus arrived at the stop, 6:30pm, the sun was setting in the late summer heat and everyone piled onto the bus. It was a different crowd, he only recognised a few faces. 
Neil sat and scanned the faces getting on he was relieved when he didn’t see Rook get on. 
Tully from the morning bus ride sat next to Neil, he hadn’t realised just how large Tully was in the morning, he was as tall as Neil, but he must have been at least 240 pounds of muscle.
Tully extended his hand “Hi, names Tully, didn’t catch yours this morning”
Neil accepted the handshake, it was a more gentle than he expected, the faint smell of oil and grease in grained in Tully’s hand hit Neil’s nose “Neil, good to meet you”
Tully asked “They’ve got you over in Stratum Projects, very cushy, everyone wants an office job” he spread his hands wide for Neil to see, the black line under his nails made it clear he got dirty for his job “How’d you swing that?”
Neil shook his head “I have absolutely no idea”
Tully laughed “I have a feeling you’ll find out soon enough… now if you don’t mind I’m going to get some shut eye, us factory workers don’t get to sit down all day in air-conditioned comfort”
Neil wanted to ask what Tully meant, but it was clear the conversation was over, he sat in silence for the rest of the ride, Tully softly snoring beside him.</span></span></span></span>

Jim’s day, and life was spiralling out of control.
Get it together, now! he told himself
Take stock of the situation and come up with a plan, he’d always backed himself and now wasn’t the time to buckle under the pressure. Where to start though, the job at Novas was gone as was his new Level 8 status. 
At least he was still a Level 7 and if he had to wait out year living like a monk as a Disruptive Person, he could do that. Jim had worked his way up from the lower levels in the Outer, so living as a Level 7 was never going be problem..
Jim was moving forward again, just like his mind was pushing forward with plans he got his car moving too, with nowhere else to go home seemed like a good option right now.
With a destination locked into his EV, Jim could relax a little and consider his situation further. 
His old job at Landis was burnt, but his skills still had to be in demand. He might have to take a few steps back down the corporate ladder, but Jim was sure he’d find a place to recover and quietly work his way back up. After all that’s what the system allowed, you might make a mistake and get a fine or a sanction, but do the right thing, be an outstanding member of society again and all was forgiven. 
Who did he know from before his days at Landis?
Jim was scrolling his contact list when a message came through from Sarah
Fuck, that was not a conversation he wanted to have now.
He had his car read it
“What did you do????? I can’t be around you at the moment, I’m going to my parents until this blows over”
There no way Sarah would have known about the incident at Apex, but she would have been alerted by his change of Status and being named a Disruptive, you can’t hid something like that.
He dictated a text back “Don’t leave, we can sort this out, it’s only a temporary sanction, I’m sure Shane can help smooth it all over, let’s talk when I get back, I’m on my way home now”
Almost immediately there was a reply “THIS WON”T SMOOTH OVER”
Followed by a second text with a just a link.
Jim opened it on the flat panel console in his car, a video started playing. 
His blood ran cold as he realised is was a video of him at the Apex restaurant, drunk and insulting the wait staff in all his new Level 8 arrogance “…Fucking idiot, you’ve just spilled a thousand dollar glass of wine over a contract worth more money than you could even imagine, are you sorry about that…” Jim was waving the wine stained contract right on the waitresses face, the wet pages slapping her “See that, it’s a real job, nothing like you’ll ever get you fucking Troff”
The video paused on close-up of Jim’s face full of rage and righteous indignation and a voice over started in a heavily synthesised voice.
“This is how the so-called Elites treat the workers, sipping expensive wine whilst abusing honest hard working staff who just want to get do thier jobs. Nothing will stop them from belittling and degrading you, These Elite want nothing more holding you all down in the Outer forever. Never forget we outnumber them. We are the Grey”
Mercifully the screen went blank.
Fuck, Fuck, Fuck. If Jim was driving he’d have crashed the car by now.
He texted Sarah back “We can fix this”
The response, again, was instant “No WE can’t, I can’t be around a Disruptive, don’t call me again or I’ll get a restraining order”
Jim was floored, he and Sarah had worked so hard together as a team to climb the ladder. He knew she was super ambitious, but so was he and it was a good match. He didn’t think she’d drop him cold like this.</span></span></span></span>

No one would have known the turmoil inside.
Jim was slumped in the luxurious leather seat replaying the video of his outburst at Apex over and over. 
Who the hell are the Greys? He’d never heard of them, he tried think back to his time in the Outer after he’d left his parents comfortable, but unambitious, level 5 home to strike out on his own. 
Then it struck him like lightning bolt, he did recognise the name, it was on one of the restricted newscasts he was able to see after Shane’s guy chipped his TV. He’d have  see if he could look it up when he got home. 
All he could remember was they were some sort of loose group of agitators born out of the Level 3’s and 4’s in the Outer who were complaining about thier lot in life. All they had to do was work hard and climb the ladder instead of complaining the newscast commentator had said at the time.
Jim watched it again and again, but not one single piece of footage showed Rob on the other side of the table, it was if someone was filming over Rob’s shoulder, but how could they do that?
His phone pinged again with a message from his PCP
Seriously, what now? Jim thought as he opened the message.
“Dear Jim Dalton, you have been issued a number of warnings: 
(1) Serious Citizenship misconduct: Associating with a Banned Group
(2) Serious Citizenship misconduct: Common Assault
(3) Serious Citizenship misconduct: Drunk and disorderly in a public place
You are hereby summoned to a hearing at the District Citizenship Court, details will be forwarded directly to your lawyer on record.
Due to the serious nature of the offence, your Citizenship Status points have been suspended temporarily and you have been reallocated to Level 5 – Restricted citizen (Temporary) 
To view more details, login to your portal.”
Numb to the constant hits he’d received today Jim just shook his head in disgust. All the plans he’d been making and the effort he’d made step back from the brink were wasted, he was ruined and there was nothing he could do.
As the grim reality of his situation settled on Jim, his car alerted to an issue and gently pulled to the side of the road. 
All I want to do is get home and crawl up into a ball, I don’t need this.
He looked at the console to see what the issue was, a red flashing message was had replaced the slick top of the line interface
[This Vehicle has been disabled by central control.
The registered owner of this vehicle is not longer considered able to fulfil the payment schedule as required.
The financial institution has repossessed this vehicle and an appointed transportation service will arrived at this location to take possession of this vehicle]
The car door opened by itself, almost inviting Jim to leave it. 
Jim just started laughing uncontrollably, a laughter that was tinged with anger and despair at the same time.
He slowly got out of the car, why rush there was nothing left for him to loose.
He was still about 10 miles from his house, normally a 15 min drive, but on foot, he didn’t know.
With a sigh he patted the car a fond farewell and started walking.</span></span></span></span>

Honeslty Jim though, walking with his own thoughts was the best thing he could be doing right now.
Luckily he’d passed out of the city proper before he got kicked out of his car, no his any longer he reminded himself. The hustle and bustle of the city and the busy main roads had been replaced by the Green. It was a rich and verdant suburbia, row upon row of houses that shared the same handful of designers, alternating architectural styles for miles on end, all with small but neat and tidy front gardens that the owners could justifiably be proud of. 
The Green stretched for miles and surrounded the city’s centre like a verdant suburban moat. It was where the bulk of the population lived, Level 6’s and 7’s and for most it was more than enough.
For Jim, now on foot forced to take the time to look at these houses instead of ignoring them as they sped by out the window, it was never enough, his ambition had burned brightly to reach the very top. He had too, if for only a week, then it had all been ripped away from him.
Getting drunk and being rude to wait staff did not justify the sanctions he faced, not even close. He couldn’t help but feel a heavy hand pushing the scales down against him.
He’d taken off his coat and tie and rolled up his sleeves, the afternoon sun was too warm to be out walking, even more so in his expensive tailored suit. The sweat starting to soak his brand new crisp white real cotton shirt, his face flushed and red from the unexpected effort.
The quiet of the walk let Jim think properly for the first time. He had so many questions. 
Who had recorded the footage? He thought Shane’s points lawyer had smoothed it all over, apparently not. What was going on with Shane’s number he wondered, he’d tried calling a few more time with the same message.
Why did the Grey choose him to ruin today? He wasn’t even sure who they were, but they’d taken situation he could handle and blown it up to ruin Jim’s life. 
 Jim was forming another plan as he walked, one way or the other, he was going to find out who did this too him.
He checked his watch, it had been about two hours so far, he reckoned he had about an hour of walking to go before he got home. His once new suit was damp with sweat, thankfully the evening was on it’s way and the sun’s heat was dropping to be replaced by a cooling breeze.
Jim remebered he’d switched his phone to do not disturb when he started walking, he just couldn’t handle any more messages. He took it out of pocket and switched it back, here’s goes nothing he thought with apprehension.
Messages flooded in, five, ten and then twenty and more, text and voice. Finally it stopped and Jim nervously scanned them,searching for anything from Sarah, but there was nothing. Mercifully there was also nothing from his PCP.
There rest were all unknown numbers, cautiously he opened the first one and listened to it
“Hello Jim, can I call you Jim? it Brad here from The Daily Outlet, I just wanted to talk to you about the video of you at Apex, call me back”
Then the next one “Mr Dalton is Sophie here from the News at 7, we’ve got some questions about your association with the Greys, can you tell us how long you’ve been a member? Call me back urgently”
Another one “Hi Jim, it’s Steve here from Citadel News Feed, we’ve love to let you put your side of the story, w’ll give you a whole hour. Please call me back before you call anyone else”
Fuck, Jim’s simply hadn’t anticipated becoming a national news story.
He read some of the texts, all the same, ugerent demands for him to call back one media outlet after another.</span></span></span></span>

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Here's the full length version of section 1 of chapter 7 : Jim was walking, not something he was used to doing, for years he’d only commuted in air-conditioned cars, so walking the 10 or so miles to his house was proving to be harder than he thought.
Just like everything else today, this was not what he expected to be doing, forced to walk home in shame.
Honeslty Jim though, walking with his own thoughts was the best thing he could be doing right now.
Luckily he’d passed out of the city proper before he got kicked out of his car, no his any longer he reminded himself. The hustle and bustle of the city and the busy main roads had been replaced by the Green. It was a rich and verdant suburbia, row upon row of houses that shared the same handful of designers, alternating architectural styles for miles on end, all with small but neat and tidy front gardens that the owners could justifiably be proud of. 
The Green stretched for miles and surrounded the city’s centre like a verdant suburban moat. It was where the bulk of the population lived, Level 6’s and 7’s and for most it was more than enough.
For Jim, now on foot forced to take the time to look at these houses instead of ignoring them as they sped by out the window, it was never enough, his ambition had burned brightly to reach the very top. He had too, if for only a week, then it had all been ripped away from him.
Getting drunk and being rude to wait staff did not justify the sanctions he faced, not even close. He couldn’t help but feel a heavy hand pushing the scales down against him.
He’d taken off his coat and tie and rolled up his sleeves, the afternoon sun was too warm to be out walking, even more so in his expensive tailored suit. The sweat starting to soak his brand new crisp white real cotton shirt, his face flushed and red from the unexpected effort.
The quiet of the walk let Jim think properly for the first time. He had so many questions. 
Who had recorded the footage? He thought Shane’s points lawyer had smoothed it all over, apparently not. What was going on with Shane’s number he wondered, he’d tried calling a few more time with the same message.
Why did the Grey choose him to ruin today? He wasn’t even sure who they were, but they’d taken situation he could handle and blown it up to ruin Jim’s life. 
 Jim was forming another plan as he walked, one way or the other, he was going to find out who did this too him.
He checked his watch, it had been about two hours so far, he reckoned he had about an hour of walking to go before he got home. His once new suit was damp with sweat, thankfully the evening was on it’s way and the sun’s heat was dropping to be replaced by a cooling breeze.
Jim remebered he’d switched his phone to do not disturb when he started walking, he just couldn’t handle any more messages. He took it out of pocket and switched it back, here’s goes nothing he thought with apprehension.
Messages flooded in, five, ten and then twenty and more, text and voice. Finally it stopped and Jim nervously scanned them,searching for anything from Sarah, but there was nothing. Mercifully there was also nothing from his PCP.
There rest were all unknown numbers, cautiously he opened the first one and listened to it
“Hello Jim, can I call you Jim? it Brad here from The Daily Outlet, I just wanted to talk to you about the video of you at Apex, call me back”
Then the next one “Mr Dalton is Sophie here from the News at 7, we’ve got some questions about your association with the Greys, can you tell us how long you’ve been a member? Call me back urgently”
Another one “Hi Jim, it’s Steve here from Citadel News Feed, we’ve love to let you put your side of the story, w’ll give you a whole hour. Please call me back before you call anyone else”
Fuck, Jim’s simply hadn’t anticipated becoming a national news story.
He read some of the texts, all the same, urgent demands for him to call back one media outlet after another.
He recognised a text from his sports club, he knew what it was going to be before he even read it
“Mr Dalton, the board of the The Willow Creek Club and has decided to revoke your membership. Please arrange with the Club Secretary to come in and pick up your personal items.”
Jim had strived for years to get into the Club, it wasn’t a guarantee even when he was a Level 7, it took Jim and Sarah a few years before they’d done enough networking to even get a spot on the waiting list.
He understood now he’d been sudden shunted down to Level 5 he was being stripped of his membership, but it didn’t ease the blow of so much time and effort in getting his membership just being discarded in a two sentence text.
Jim continued walking, the well planned suburbia had been replaced by a neat and tide small shopping village, the kind Jim and Sarah went to every weekend. It wasn’t one of the huge malls that dominated the closer you go to the Outer, this was just for the locals. 
He spotted a connivence store, Yes! he thought.
Jim had forgotten that he’d only had his morning coffee at home,, the sight of the shops and the convenience store instantly reminded him just how thirsty, and hungry he was. He didn’t need to be anywhere right now so a quick strop wouldn’t hurt him.
He was about 30 minutes away from his house and never came to this village so no chance anyone would recognise him. Jim tucked in his shirt, ran his fingers through his hair and tried to make himself as presentable as he could.
Jim walked in and immediately felt the welcome chill of the air-conditioning, he nodded to the cashier how proceeded to completely ignore him. The Convention store was tastefully sized, deliberately just big enough that you could get almost everything you needed without having to venture further afield to a big box supermarket. 
Jim went straight for the drink fridge at the back of the store, his thirst seemed to increase the closer he got. Force of habit had him reaching for a sparkling water, but he paused what was the point, today of all days, to be careful of his calory points tracker. He put back the water and moved over to the soft drink fridge, it had been a while since he’d had a guilt free soft drink. 
He was pondering the flavours when he spotted beer a few fridge doors over, Hell yes! Jim took one cold beer, stopped and took another, it wasn’t as if he had anything to loose today. 
There was TV playing music videos just above the row of fridges and he glanced at it “NEWS ALERT” flashed across the screen.
The new anchor spoke “Interrupting your scheduled programming with this breaking new alert as we follow the story of Jim Dalton, a former Level 8 executive now sanctioned down to Level 5 after the so-called Greys, a little known disruptive group who released the now viral footage of a drunken Dalton abusing and assaulting wait staff in an exclusive restaurant earlier this morning”
The news was showing the footage of Jim at the Apex restaurant in the background.
“We have Tanner Holt on the ground with a breaking update, Tanner what’s new information have you got for us”
Tanner is standing out on the street in front of what looks like Jim’s car “Thanks Lina, as you know we’ve been trying to track down the elusive Mr Dalton to ask him how he is associated with the groups the Greys, and does he have any comment on assaulting wait staff the the Apex restaurant. Mr Dalotn looks to have gone to ground for now after leaving his old job at Landis Corpoartion earlier today.
Lina, just moment ago we were alerted by member of the public to this car sitting abandoned here on the side of the road about 10 miles down Trunk Road 4.”
The camera zooms in on Jim’s car, disable on the side of the road with the driver door still open.
Tanner picks up the story again “We’ve since confirmed that this car was registered to Mr Dalton up until only a few hours ago, in fact” He gestures to the man behind the camera “John, get a close-up of the console” 
John obliges and the sames message is flashing on it.
[This Vehicle has been disabled by central control.
The registered owner of this vehicle is not longer considered able to fulfil the payment schedule as required.
The financial institution has repossessed this vehicle and an appointed transportation service will arrived at this location to take possession of this vehicle]
Tanner is now offscreen and the camera stays on the message flashing in red and black on the screen “As you can see here Lina, the car was disabled and repossessed, and it looks like Dalton has just abandoned it here on the side of this busy road, Lina”
“Thanks Tanner, any sign of Mr Dalton?” 
Tanner back on camera and standing next to the open door to Jim’s car “No Lina, no sign of him here, we don’t know where he is at the moment. I’m told that both the Metro Police and the Citizenship Enforcement Bureau have active investigations open into Mr Dalton. Once source from the CEB assured me that Mr Dalton is not in any danger and they are monitoring his movements and will step in if necessary. Back to you Lina
Lina is sitting behind the news desk “This is just another worrying twist in the case of Jim Dalton, a corporate high flyer who who thought the rules didn’t apply to him, we hope he’s safe. Now over to Kira Maddox who is outside Jim Daltons home”
“Kira, any sign of Mr Dalton there?”
“Thanks Lina, I’m standing outside Mr Dalton’s luxury house in the exclusive suburb of Laurelton Park, as you can see behind me there is no sign of activity in the house at the moment, we don;t know of Mr Dalton will even come back here but we’ll be onsite to update if anything happens, back to you Lina”
“Thank you Kira, please do keep us posted. Now back your scheduled programming”
Jim was having what feels like an out of body experience, seeing his car that he was driving only a few hours ago, and his house splashed across the TV, the air-con was now too cold as he shivered with the though if his life being exposed for all to see.
Jim skulked his way to front counter having replaced the beers with a large sugary soft drink. The clerk continued to ignore Jim as he paid, Jim couldn’t get out of there quick enough.
There were at his house, what is he going to do now?</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Section 4 of chpater 7: Home finally! Jim was elated, never in his life had it been so hard to just go home. Yet here he was. 
He stood in the darkness of his yard, the low murmur of the media out front only just reaching him, the spotlight lights shining against the front of his house making it seem even darker in the backyard.
Jim, reached into pocket for his keys. They weren’t there.
Oh No he frantically patted down all of his pockets, but his keys were nowhere to be found. Had he left them in the car? Had he dropped them jumping over one of the fences?
He got down on his knees and scrabbled around where he landed to see if he’d only just dropped them. It was too dark to see anything, and after a short time Jim gave up scratching around in the garden. They were gone.
Jim was more annoyed that worried, it would have been too easy just to be able sneaking his back door, this day was really trying to test him. He knew he had a spare set of keys hidden by the side door. The side door felt a bit exposed, he really wanted to get inside without anyone knowing and keep it that way.
Just be careful Jim thought to himself as he tentatively looked around the corner to the side of the house. The picket fence and gate separating the front yard from the side of the house was a good six feet tall, but was only half timbered, so you could easily see through it. 
Jim carefully scanned his path to the side door and it seemed the media pack down by the footpath was at an ebb, no one was really looking in his direction. 
Carefully and slowly, Jim crept around the corner, sliding himself tight against the side of the house he crept the 15 or so meters to the side door. The key was under a pot just across from the door. From the indent of the side door he looked again at the media, no one was paying attention, he snuck over to the pot and knelt down behind it. The pot didn’t provide any cover really, it was only a foot tall and empty. 
Jim gently tilted it and felt under the pot, where was this key? His hand couldn’t find it so he tipped the pot further and bent over to look under.
There it was, stuck to the bottom of the pot with the dirt, it had been a while since he’d needed to use it. Jim grabbed for the key, the pot tipped over too far and he lost control of it. It clattered over and smashed into a dozen or so pieces.
No! The noise sounded deafening to Jim crouched on his knees in the quiet at the side of his house. Panicked he looked up and through the fence. It felt like the media turned as one to look towards the house, the low hum of mundane conversation of the bored media pack rose a pitch. Someone trained a spotlight to where the sound had come from. Jim could see the zebra petter of light and shadow on the ground and him.
He held deathly still, perhaps they couldn’t see him.
A voice yelled out “There’s someone there!” 
Shit, it was a that moment he realised he didn’t have the key in his hand, it was somewhere under the debris of the broken pot and the soil that it held now spread over the side path.
cameramen and reporters were now in a mad dash to his side gate with reporters and camera operators elbowing each other out of the way to get the best shots.
Jim was frantically pushing the broken pieces of terracotta around trying to find the key, he cut his hand on one of the shards and started adding his own blood to the soil.
The first camera man got to the gate stopped to leaned his camera over it and get the shot, but the gate opened and he fell into onto the path directly in front of Jim. Now the gate was open, the pack rushed in with not regard for Jim or the cameraman on the ground.
Jim was light up be a dozen camera mounted lights and the reporters were screaming questions at him at the same time
“Mr Dalton are you a member of the Greys?’
“Mr Dalton why did you assault the waitress?”
“Are you a danger to society”
“What’s it like being designated a disruptive Person?”
Jim’s hand found the key finally and he stood up, his pants covered in mud and dirt, his had red with blood, he eyes squinting starting into the lights.
The throng had surrounded him and were jostling him like he was in a washing machine, he had no choice but to push through them to get to the side door if his house.
Jim pushed but they didn’t move, he pushed again but they were shoulder to should in the tight space.
Jim yelled at them “Get out of my way, get off my property!” and pushed through again. He was hit in the face by one microphone, then another .
A cameraman had backed up into the doorway and Jim yelled again “Move!”
He didn’t.
Jim needed to get inside.
He grabbed cameraman and shoved him are hard as he could off the small stoop of the side door. The man went sprawling into the narrow garden between the side path and the house. His camera flew off onto the pathway smashing into pieces, all the other camera’s capturing the moment the man and the camera hit the ground.
Jim didn’t have time to see any of that, he showed the key into the lock and burst into house slamming the door shut behind him with a force that rattled the windows.
Jim collapsed onto the floor exhausted, he was spent, he didn’t even register the banging on the door as the adrenalin left his body and he passed out lying there on the cold floor in his dark house.</span></span></span></span>
